Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: DR Congo's "Digital Code" (Ordonnance-Loi No. 23/010 of 13 March 2023) includes general personal data protection provisions that cover processing of payment and billing data; a dedicated payment-data-specific regime was not evidenced. [DLA Piper Data Protection Laws (DRC)](https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=law&c=CD);[Digital Watch Observatory summary](https://dig.watch/resource/democratic-republic-of-the-congos-digital-code)
revision_notes: Both cited sources were fetched and confirmed current: DRC's Digital Code (Ordonnance-Loi No. 23/010 of 13 March 2023, in force since 13 March 2023, published 11 April 2023) establishes general personal data protection provisions (Articles 126, 131-133) applicable to all data controllers, and its e-commerce title (Article 48) explicitly extends these rules to providers of mobile and electronic payment services, credit institutions and microfinance institutions. A supplementary Lexing.be legal analysis corroborates this and notes an earlier 2020 Telecommunications Law also contained data-protection provisions, plus DRC's 2025 ratification of the AU Malabo Convention. No DRC legislation was found containing provisions specific to payment transaction data (which would warrant code 3); the regime remains general data protection law applied to the payments sector. The general/comprehensive vs sector-specific distinction supports retaining the original score.
revised_comments: DR Congo's data protection framework rests on the Digital Code (Ordonnance-Loi No. 23/010 of 13 March 2023), which entered into force on 13 March 2023 and was published in the official journal on 11 April 2023. The Code establishes general personal data protection rights (confidentiality, consent, restrictions on processing of sensitive categories) applicable across sectors, and its e-commerce provisions explicitly bring providers of mobile and electronic payment services, credit institutions and microfinance institutions within its scope. An earlier Telecommunications Law of 2020 also contained data-protection provisions later reinforced by the Digital Code. No dedicated legal regime specific to payment transaction data exists; payment data is covered only under this general data protection framework.
